# TensileLite characterization-test dev env

A **fully reproducible** local environment for the TensileLite
characterization work. CPU-only (no GPU needed for the `unit` group).
Local-only; no push.

The base ROCm image is generated by the **`rocm` skill** from the
`engex-marketplace-internal` plugin marketplace (`/rocm:env`), which
fetches TheRock CI artifacts from a public S3 bucket by run id and stages
them onto TheRock's manylinux base. Everything is built from public
sources — no privately-loaded image.

Validated end-to-end on 2026-06-03 with `tensilelite-char:repro`:
- image builds (14.3 GB),
- `invoke rocisa` builds + imports cleanly,
- `pytest -m unit Tensile/Tests/unit` → **1974 passed, 201 skipped,
  610 snapshots passed** (exit 0),
- coverage path-mode (`--cov=<dir>`) runs without the nanobind abort.

---

## What changed and why (read this first)

The previous env did `FROM rocm-libs-bump-e3b:26531351157`. That tag is a
**TheRock CI build artifact** loaded locally (labels:
`source=github.com/ROCm/TheRock`, `therock.run_id=26531351157`,
`therock.arch=gfx94X-dcgpu`). It was produced by one GitHub Actions run
and **cannot be rebuilt from a Dockerfile** — nobody else has the tag and
the run's artifacts eventually expire.

This env reconstructs an **equivalent** base from public sources via the
`rocm` skill. The pinned build:

| field          | value                                        |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| TheRock run id | `26531351157`                                |
| TheRock SHA    | `94675052fd427fd2cc6ec9180079b3a0dc7d26b2`   |
| GPU family     | `gfx94X-dcgpu` (gfx942 / MI300)              |

---

## 1. Generate the base image with the `rocm` skill (recommended)

The `rocm` skill lives in **engex-marketplace-internal**:
<https://github.com/ROCm/engex-marketplace-internal> (private; needs
GitHub access). Its `/rocm:env` command and `build-dev-env` agent automate
the whole "fetch TheRock artifacts → write Dockerfile → build image" flow.

### Install the plugin (once)

In Claude Code:

```text
# Add the experimental marketplace, then install the rocm plugin:
/plugin marketplace add ROCm/engex-marketplace-internal@experimental
/plugin install rocm@engex-experimental

# (or from a local clone)
/plugin marketplace add /path/to/engex-marketplace-internal
```

Docs: `/rocm:env --help` and `/rocm:help` for the full surface. The
marketplace README covers install/use/develop.

### Generate the env

```text
# Fetch this run's artifacts + write the canonical manylinux Dockerfile,
# then build the image in one step:
/rocm:env --build --arch gfx94X-dcgpu --source run:26531351157 \
          --name tensilelite-char

# Useful neighbors:
/rocm:env --builds                 # list candidate CI runs (-> --source run:<id>)
/rocm:env --analyze                # pick the run rocm-libraries currently pins
/rocm:env --inspect --name tensilelite-char   # show provenance labels
```

That gives you a working ROCm base. To add the characterization test
layer (Python deps incl. syrupy + rocisa's runtime env vars), either:

- pass `--no-build` to `/rocm:env --build` and append the Layer-B block
  from the committed `Dockerfile` (below) to the generated one, or
- just use the committed `Dockerfile` directly — §2 — which already
  contains both layers and is the exact output of this skill plus that
  layer.

Then continue at §3 (get source) → §6 (run tests).

---

## 2. Build from the committed `Dockerfile` (the env we already generated)

This directory already holds the end-to-end `Dockerfile` — Layer A is the
`/rocm:env` manylinux output for run `26531351157`, Layer B is the
characterization test layer. You only need to stage the artifacts the
`COPY` step expects, then build.

### 2a. Stage the ROCm artifacts into the build context

The `Dockerfile` does `COPY artifacts/ /opt/rocm-pkg/`, so the build
context (this dir) must contain an `artifacts/` tree (~8.3 GB,
**not** committed). Get it one of two ways:

**Via the skill** (what §1 automates), then hardlink it next to this
`Dockerfile`:

```sh
ENV=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/work/tensilelite-characterization/env
# after /rocm:env --build ... --no-build --output-dir <DIR>:
cp -al <DIR>/artifacts "$ENV/artifacts"      # hardlinks; instant
```

**Manually** (exactly what the skill does under the hood):

```sh
ENV=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/work/tensilelite-characterization/env

# Confirm the run still has artifacts in S3 (non-empty = good):
curl -fsSL \
  "https://therock-ci-artifacts.s3.amazonaws.com/?prefix=26531351157-linux/&max-keys=5" \
  | grep -oE '<Key>[^<]+' | head

# Shallow-clone TheRock at the run's SHA (matches artifact taxonomy):
THEROCK_TMP=$(mktemp -d)
git -C "$THEROCK_TMP" init -q
git -C "$THEROCK_TMP" remote add origin https://github.com/ROCm/TheRock.git
git -C "$THEROCK_TMP" fetch --depth=1 -q origin 94675052fd427fd2cc6ec9180079b3a0dc7d26b2
git -C "$THEROCK_TMP" checkout -q FETCH_HEAD

# Fetch artifacts into the build context (unauthenticated; env -u strips
# any ambient GitHub token so none leaks into the build):
mkdir -p "$ENV/artifacts"
env -u GH_TOKEN -u GITHUB_TOKEN \
python3 "$THEROCK_TMP/build_tools/fetch_artifacts.py" \
  --run-id=26531351157 \
  --artifact-group=gfx94X-dcgpu \
  --amdgpu-targets=gfx942 \
  --output-dir="$ENV/artifacts" \
  --flatten \
  '(core-(hip|runtime|kpack|ocl|amdsmi|hipinfo)|amd-llvm|sysdeps|base|rocprofiler-(sdk|compute|systems)|host-(blas|suite-sparse)|hipblaslt|blas|rand|fft|prim|rocwmma|miopen|miopenprovider|rccl|mpi|rocdecode|rocjpeg|aqlprofile|hipdnn|libhipcxx)_(lib|dev|run)'

rm -rf "$THEROCK_TMP"
```

Either way `"$ENV/artifacts"` ends up with `bin/`, `lib/`, `include/`
(`lib/libamdhip64.so.7` is a good sentinel). `artifacts/` is git-ignored
here, so it won't pollute the tree.

### 2b. Build the image

```sh
DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 docker build -t tensilelite-char:repro "$ENV"
```

First build sends the ~8.3 GB context to the daemon; rebuilds reuse
layers. (The `Dockerfile` deliberately omits a `# syntax=` directive so
BuildKit doesn't try to pull a frontend image from docker.io — that pull
401s on hosts without docker.io auth.)

---

## 3. Get the source

The characterization tests, this env, and the `shared/origami` +
`shared/stinkytofu` siblings rocisa needs are all in the one monorepo —
a plain clone gets everything (no submodule init).

```sh
git clone git@github.com:ROCm/rocm-libraries.git
cd rocm-libraries
git checkout users/davidd-amd/tensillite-coverage
```

(If you are reading this file, you already have the checkout.)

---

## 4. Start a persistent container with the worktree mounted

The worktree root must be mounted so `shared/origami` +
`shared/stinkytofu` resolve for rocisa's CMake.

```sh
WT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
TL=projects/hipblaslt/tensilelite
docker rm -f tl-char 2>/dev/null
docker run -d --name tl-char \
  -v "$WT":/work -w /work/$TL \
  tensilelite-char:repro sleep infinity
```

(GPU is not needed for the `unit` group. If you later run client/GPU
paths, add `--device=/dev/kfd --device=/dev/dri --group-add video`.)

---

## 5. Build rocisa once (inside the container)

rocisa is **not** baked into the image — its CMake links the monorepo
siblings, which live in the worktree. Build it editable, once:

```sh
docker exec -w /work/$TL tl-char invoke rocisa
docker exec tl-char python3 -c \
  "import rocisa; from rocisa.enum import DataTypeEnum; print('rocisa OK')"
```

The `_rocisa.so` + CMake build tree live in the worktree (`$TL/rocisa/`),
so they persist across container runs. `ROCM_PATH` and
`LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/rocm/lib` are baked into the image, so
`import rocisa` works in plain (non-login) `docker exec`.

---

## 6. Run characterization / coverage

Full suite (no-regression check — same invocation as upstream):

```sh
docker exec -w /work/$TL tl-char \
  pytest -m unit Tensile/Tests/unit
```

Expect ~1974 passed / 201 skipped / 610 snapshots passed.

Coverage scoped to a target component:

```sh
docker exec -w /work/$TL tl-char \
  pytest -m unit \
    --cov=Tensile/SolutionStructs/Validators \
    --cov-config=pyproject.toml --cov-report=term-missing \
    Tensile/Tests/unit
```

> ⚠️ **Coverage gotcha.** Pass `--cov` a value that resolves to an
> existing **directory** (run from `$TL`, so `Tensile/SolutionStructs/...`
> resolves). Coverage uses path mode when the arg matches a dir, but
> *imports* the arg as a module when it doesn't — and importing a
> rocisa-touching module re-initializes the `_rocisa` nanobind extension
> → `nanobind: refusing to add duplicate key` → SIGABRT (core dump,
> empty output). So `--cov=Tensile.SolutionStructs.Validators` (dotted,
> no matching path) aborts; the **dir path** does not.

---

## Notes

### syrupy

The characterization tests are **syrupy** snapshot tests
(`assert result == snapshot`, with committed `__snapshots__/*.ambr`
files). `syrupy` is now declared in the repo's test deps — `tox.ini`
(`[testenv]` + `pre_commit`) and `pyproject.toml` (`[dependency-groups].dev`)
— so a clean checkout can run the suite via the normal install. The image
also pins it directly so it is self-sufficient.

### Optional: a fully-baked, mount-free image

`docker commit tl-char tensilelite-char:rocisa` snapshots rocisa into the
image. Caveat: an **editable** rocisa keeps build-tree rpaths /
`_build_info` pointing into the mounted worktree, so the committed image
still needs that mount. A truly portable image would need a non-editable
`pip install ./rocisa` with static origami/stinkytofu — not validated.

### Re-pinning to a newer ROCm

Pick a new run id (`/rocm:env --builds` or `--analyze`), update the three
`LABEL` lines + the SHA/run-id in the `Dockerfile` and §2, re-fetch
`artifacts/`, rebuild. Nothing else changes.
